userStories.title: internal/llm/pockettts Go HTTP client (mirrors whisper/client.go)
userStories.description: Add the Go HTTP client wrapping the aura-pocket-tts sidecar /tts endpoint. Mirrors `internal/llm/whisper/client.go` shape: thread-safe Client struct, New constructor with baseURL/timeout/logger, single Synthesize method, ≤200-char body excerpt on non-200, no leaked secrets. (a) NEW package `internal/llm/pockettts/`. File `client.go` (~150 LOC). Type `SynthesizeResult struct { Audio []byte; MimeType string; ElapsedMs int; Voice string; Language string }`. Type `Client struct { baseURL string; httpc *http.Client; logger *slog.Logger; defaultVoice string; defaultLanguage string }`. Constructor `func New(baseURL string, timeout time.Duration, logger *slog.Logger) *Client` with sensible defaults: defaultVoice="giovanni", defaultLanguage="italian_24l". (b) Method `func (c *Client) Synthesize(ctx context.Context, text string, voice string) (SynthesizeResult, error)`. If voice is empty, use c.defaultVoice. Builds a multipart/form-data POST to `<baseURL>/tts` with fields `text` (the prompt) + `voice_url` (the built-in voice name). Reads the streaming response body into a buffer with `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 8*1024*1024))` — 8 MB cap is generous for a single TTS reply (giovanni @ 24 kHz mono s16le = ~48 KB/sec; 8 MB = ~170 sec of audio, far beyond any Telegram voice message). Returns SynthesizeResult populated with the audio bytes, MimeType="audio/wav", ElapsedMs measured around the HTTP round-trip, Voice + Language echoed back from the request. On non-200: error message includes status code + first 200 chars of body (no full upstream body leaked). (c) Edge cases: empty text → return ErrEmptyText (`errors.New("pockettts: empty text")`); ctx cancellation propagates via http.NewRequestWithContext; baseURL missing trailing logic — match whisper/client.go (it just concatenates `baseURL+"/tts"`, so the caller must pass `http://host:port` without trailing slash). (d) File `client_test.go` (~120 LOC) — table-driven tests using httptest.NewServer that simulate: (i) happy path: server returns 200 + WAV-magic header bytes (`RIFF....WAVE...`), Synthesize returns matching SynthesizeResult with ElapsedMs >= 0; (ii) non-200: server returns 500 + body "upstream busy", Synthesize returns error with substring `pockettts: server 500: upstream busy`; (iii) empty text rejected before HTTP call; (iv) ctx cancellation cancels in-flight request; (v) body exceeds 8 MB cap → truncated cleanly via LimitReader (verify the captured payload size). NO real network calls — all tests hit httptest. (e) Configuration glue: add a getter in `internal/config/applier.go` (or wherever sidecar URLs are read) for `POCKETTTS_BASE_URL` env (default empty — disabled when unset). DO NOT instantiate the client globally in this story; that's A07's job. Just expose the constructor + the config read so A07 can wire it. (f) THIS STORY WIRES NOTHING INTO THE AGENT LOOP. No tool registration. No outbound integration. No /voice command. Just the package + tests + config read.

The three modes are: `off` = text only (default); `voice_only` = synth voice + suppress text in the Telegram reply; `all` = synth voice IN ADDITION to text (hermes pattern — voice augments text, never replaces it... except when user explicitly picks voice_only). userStories.title: Wire pocket-tts into Telegram outbound — TTS additive to text
userStories.description: Connect A05 (pockettts.Client) + A06 (audio.Policy) into the Telegram outbound flow so a chat with voice_mode=all gets text + voice, voice_mode=voice_only gets voice only, and voice_mode=off (default) is unchanged. (a) Plumbing: internal/channels/telegram/outbound.go gains two new injected dependencies on the Outbound struct: `tts *pockettts.Client` (nil-safe — if nil, TTS is globally disabled) + `policy audio.Store`. Update the constructor to accept them. (b) Decision point: in the outbound message dispatch (find `bot.Send` or `bot.Edit` for the final reply text — grep `sendRemainder` and `editMessage` plus wherever the FIRST chunk is sent for the streaming path; the final-text-rendered point is where the decision lives). After (or alongside) the text send: (i) read policy mode via `o.policy.Get(ctx, chatID)`; (ii) if Mode=off → unchanged behavior, return; (iii) if Mode=all → text already sent above, now synth + Voice.Send the audio additively (synth failure logs at WARN and does NOT delete or modify the text reply); (iv) if Mode=voice_only → synth FIRST then send Voice; if synth succeeds, suppress the text by SKIPPING the bot.Send for the text; if synth fails, FALL BACK to sending text (degraded mode — never leave the user with no reply). Implementation knob: a helper `o.maybeSpeak(ctx, recipient, chatID, finalText)` that encapsulates the decision and either returns true (text already covered by voice_only) or false (text still needed). (c) Telegram Voice API: use `bot.Send(recipient, &tele.Voice{File: tele.FromReader(bytes.NewReader(audio))})` — the bot's tele.Voice type accepts an io.Reader via tele.FromReader. Voice messages are limited to ~50 MB on Telegram; the pockettts client's 8 MB cap is well under. (d) Failure modes that must NOT block text: synth timeout, sidecar 500, sidecar unhealthy, ctx cancel mid-synth, sidecar URL empty (TTS not configured) — all log at WARN with `tts_dispatch_failed` + reason, then fall through to text. The text reply is the source of truth — TTS is a bonus. (e) Tests: outbound_test.go gains TestOutbound_VoiceMode_Off_NoSynth, TestOutbound_VoiceMode_All_SendsBoth, TestOutbound_VoiceMode_VoiceOnly_SuppressesText, TestOutbound_VoiceMode_VoiceOnly_FailureFallsBackToText, TestOutbound_TTSNotConfigured_OffByDefault. Use a mock pockettts.Client (or a httptest wrapper) returning canned audio bytes. (f) NO probe_chat case in this story — that's A08. NO web-chat surface — Telegram only.

(c) The case ALSO inspects the actual audio bytes (NOT just the count) — fetches the buffered audio (either from a test-mode in-memory capture that the probe enables OR from the sibling table's optional dump path) and asserts the WAV magic header `RIFF....WAVE` is present.
